newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks to take direction from data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks to take direction from data.

text.p: Wall Street stocks will take their cue from March economic data at the start of trading Wednesday after a Dow rally yesterday managed to erase the average's losses from last week.
But analysts said it would take more than one rally and one piece of economic data, in Tuesday's case, the March CPI, to convince investors that momentum was turning around.
March housing starts are expected at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT while industrial production and capacity utilization are due out at 0915 EDT/1315 GMT.

"The Fed is not influenced by the PPI and CPI but by the vigor of the economy which could lead to future inflation," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities. "It will be more influenced by the data today. Housing starts will be lower because February was seasonally strong.
"There has been no major followthrough (to yesterday's rally) in Europe. We may have had the second largest point gain, but on a percentage basis it wasn't even in the top 50," he added.
Wachtel said that overseas strength in shares of Philip Morris Cos Inc would give the Dow a boost.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average climbed 97.61 points, or 0.54 percent, to close at 18,031.20.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was up 4.3 at 4291.1.
U.S. tobacco stocks led most others higher in London on Wednesday after reports of secret talks over a settlement of the tobacco industry's liabilities.

The Wall Street Journal said Philip Morris and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp were in talks which could lead to the elimination of nearly all the industry's liability, in return for strict advertising curbs and a payment of up to $300 billion over the next 25 years.
Philip Morris stock was trading at $40-1/2, compared with New York's close of $38-7/8. RJR was up US$3/4 at $31.

Among other active stocks in London hi-techs bounced ahead of a batch of quarterly results from Apple Computer and AMR Corp, on Wednesday. International Business Machines Corp was trading up $1/2 at $138-3/8 and Texas Instruments Inc was $1/4 better at $84-3/4. Among the losers, Boeing Co was off 3/8 at 100-1/2.
The dollar was static in Tokyo and little changed in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were mostly lower, with the long bond down 5/32 to yield 7.11 percent.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that there is one thing holders of Tele-Communications Inc's battered stock need not worry too much about: the dumping of 40 million or so TCI shares on the market in August. That is when taxes of $500 million will be due on the estate of the cable giant's late chairman Bob Magness.
The New York Times Market Place writes that Felix G. Rohatyn, nominated U.S. ambassador to France, could leave his post as managing director and senior partner at Lazard Freres.
The move will raise questions about what Lazard Freres will be like once he is gone.
